About Neon Kit

Neon Kit is a Tailwind-based theme paired with optional Light-DOM web components. The theme provides the visual language; the web components add native interaction, keyboard behavior, and form participation for the controls that benefit from it.

What's inside

  • @neon-kit/theme — Tailwind theme tokens and component CSS.
  • @neon-kit/web-components — Light-DOM custom elements that consume the theme.

Project goals

  • Minimal runtime — ship raw CSS and unbundled JS.
  • Lean on native browser features: popover API, anchor positioning, ElementInternals.
  • No bundler lock-in — drop into any toolchain that handles ESM and CSS.

License & links

Released under the MIT license. Source on GitHub.

site/sections/combobox-multi.html.content:
Combobox — Multi-Select

Multi-select .combobox.-multi — same field/popover family as the single-select variant, but the field hosts a wrappable tag list and an inline auto-growing search input that expand the field's block size as more items are picked. Each tag carries its own .tag__remove close affordance, the popover uses .checkbox-prefixed option rows, and footer slots can host an optional "Select all" toggle and an optional "Create new …" row. RTL is handled by the same logical-property layout that single-select uses.

Plain

Click the field or focus it and press Space to open. Click options to toggle them; click a tag's × to remove it.

With Search and Select All

data-searchable mounts a sticky search header; data-select-all mounts a "Select all" toggle in the popover footer. The toggle reflects an indeterminate state when only some options are selected.

With Create New

data-creatable appends a "Create new" footer row when the search query doesn't match any existing option. Pressing Enter in the inline field also creates a tag if creation is enabled.

Everything On

Search, select-all, and create-new together. Add a few tags and watch the field grow vertically as the tag list wraps; the trailing chevron stays parked at the inline-end edge.

Field States

Same six-state vocabulary as the single-select variant. Because the multi field is a <div> rather than a <button>, "disabled" is opted into via aria-disabled="true" on the .combobox__field; tag × affordances stay rendered but become inert. Read-only paints the muted surface and locks tag removal at the JS level (CSS just handles appearance). Invalid uses the shared aria-invalid="true" hook with a .field-error helper.

RTL

Tags wrap inline-start to inline-end; the chevron parks at the inline-end (visually left in RTL); the popover anchors from the field's bottom-start edge.

site/sections/combobox-single.html.content:
Combobox — Single-Select

Single-select .combobox — a focusable field that opens a .menu-styled popover with one selectable option. The field reuses the inset-well language of .input; the popover reuses the panel chrome of .menu. A trailing clear button removes the current value, an optional search field filters options, and an optional "Create new" row appends an option from the typed query. Layout is logical-property based so the control flips cleanly under dir="rtl".

Plain

The minimum: a field, a chevron, and a list of options. Click the field or press Space / Enter while focused to toggle the popover.

With Clear

Adding a .combobox__clear button next to the value lets users remove the current selection without opening the popover.

With Search

A sticky .combobox__search header at the top of the popover filters the list as the user types. Empty-state row appears when the filter eliminates every option.

With Create New

data-creatable opts in to a footer row that lets users add a new option from the typed query. The footer row only appears while the query is non-empty and not already in the list.

Field States

The field shares the six-state vocabulary used by .input: empty/disabled, empty/read-only, disabled with value, read-only with value, validation error, and labelled inside a form. Disabled freezes the chevron + clear; read-only opts in via aria-readonly="true" and tints the well to the secondary surface (consumers gate the popover from opening). Invalid is opted into via aria-invalid="true" and pairs with a .field-error helper. Only the field appearance is shown here — the popover is unchanged.

RTL

Setting dir="rtl" on any ancestor flips the field, the chevron position, and the popover anchor side — no per-component code required.

The user picks the first endpoint, navigates to bring the second one into view if needed (next month / year / decade via the existing header), then picks the second endpoint. While the second pick is pending, the wrapper carries .-range-pending and the band follows the cursor as a tentative preview; once committed, the band is rendered from the stored start/end pair.

site/sections/datepicker.html.content:
Datepicker

A typeable date field paired with a popover that hosts three navigable views — days inside a month, months inside a year, and years inside a decade. The field reuses the inset-well chrome of .input and the trailing-control language of .combobox: a clear button (optional) plus a calendar-icon trigger. Each cell in every view is a focusable button so the picker is fully keyboard-navigable. Layout is logical-property based; everything flips cleanly under dir="rtl".

Plain

The minimum: a typeable input and a calendar trigger that opens the day grid. Click the header label to step up to the month view, then again to the year view.

With Clear

Adding data-clearable shows a clear button when the field has a value — same affordance language as .combobox__clear.

Field States

Same six-state vocabulary every text-like control ships: empty/disabled, empty/read-only, both filled equivalents, invalid, and labelled inside a form. State hooks land on the inner .datepicker__input; the .datepicker__field wrapper reacts via :has(). Trigger and clear buttons mirror the input's disabled attribute. Only the field appearance is shown — the calendar popover is unchanged.

site/sections/forms.html.content:
Form Controls

Inputs, checkboxes, radios, and fieldsets share the visual family of .btn: same border, same focus ring, same disabled treatment. Inputs read as an inset well (you type into them) while checkboxes and radios re-use the raised .btn shape and fill with --color-primary when checked. Fieldsets are flat frames — no drop shadow — that group related fields under a small-caps legend.

Text Inputs

Apply .input to any single-line form control. Layout (width, stretch) is owned by the surrounding container — the component sets only the chrome.

Input Types

.input works on every native text-like control — email, number, search, date, file, plus <textarea> and <select>. The chevron on a styled <select> is rendered via background-image so it's consistent across browsers.

Prefix & Suffix Affixes

Wrap an .input in .input-group to render non-interactive labels — currency, units, a per-period suffix — inside the field's border. The wrapper carries the chrome (border, focus swap, disabled / read-only / invalid surfaces); the inner input drops its own border so the affix and the editable value read as a single field. Same pattern as the .timepicker__field hosting its inline timezone picker. Use a <span> for inert labels and a <button> if the affix should be interactive (e.g., a unit toggle).

Field States

Six canonical states every text-like field supports — empty disabled, empty read-only, both filled equivalents, an invalid field showing the error helper, and a labelled field inside a form. Disabled paints the muted-surface shell and freezes interaction; read-only flips to the secondary surface but stays focusable; invalid is opted into via aria-invalid="true" (the same hook native form validation toggles on submit) and pairs with a .field-error helper underneath.

Textarea & Select States

textarea.input and select.input pick up the same six-state vocabulary. Disabled freezes both; read-only flips a textarea to the muted surface while a select doesn't accept readonly natively, so consumers either lock the value with disabled or render the chosen option as non-editable text.

Checkboxes

Native <input type="checkbox"> with the UA chrome stripped and re-rendered as a small .btn-shaped square. Sized in em so the box tracks its label's font-size automatically.

Checkboxes also scale with surrounding text:

Radio Buttons

Same shape as .checkbox but circular and with a dot instead of a tick. Group radios with a shared name in the usual native way.

Fieldset

.fieldset is a flat frame for grouping related fields. Pair it with native <legend> for an accessible group label that browsers expose to assistive tech.

Notification preferences

Composed Form

Inputs, checkboxes, radios, fieldsets, and buttons composed together — everything shares the same border, focus ring, and disabled treatment.

site/sections/getting-started.html.content:
Getting Started

Neon Kit ships a Tailwind-based theme package and optional native web components. Import the theme stylesheet once in your app entry, then use the component classes in your markup.

Install the theme

pnpm add @neon-kit/theme

// In your bundle entry:
import '@neon-kit/theme/index.css';

Use the CSS components

Theme components are plain CSS classes, so they work with native elements and your framework's regular templates. 

<button class="btn cta">Save changes</button>

Add web components

Install the web component package when you want the native custom elements to manage interaction, keyboard behavior, and form participation for supported controls. 

pnpm add @neon-kit/theme @neon-kit/web-components

// In your bundle entry:
import '@neon-kit/theme/index.css';
import '@neon-kit/web-components/tooltip';

Web components render in Light DOM and do not attach shadow roots. The host page must include @neon-kit/theme/index.css or a theme-equivalent stylesheet for them to render correctly.

site/sections/icon-web-component.html.content:
Icon - Web Component

  • Library
  • Web Component

<neon-icon> is a Light-DOM custom element that renders @neon-kit/icons definitions as inline SVG. Use it when authoring HTML directly or when a component boundary makes a custom element more convenient than importing and placing SVG yourself. For package-only usage, see the Icons library.

Installation

pnpm add @neon-kit/icons @neon-kit/web-components

// Side-effect register the <neon-icon> element.
import '@neon-kit/web-components/icon';

Name loading

Set name to <variant>/<icon>, matching the icon package subpath layout. The element dynamic-imports the requested module and renders into Light DOM so it inherits currentColor. 

<neon-icon name="outline/bars-3"></neon-icon>
<neon-icon name="solid/check" label="Confirmed"></neon-icon>
outline/bars-3 solid/check mini/x-mark micro/chevron-down

Property override

For maximum tree-shaking, statically import an icon definition and assign it to the icon property. That path skips dynamic loading and takes precedence over name until cleared. 

import bars from '@neon-kit/icons/outline/bars-3';

const el = document.querySelector('neon-icon');
el.icon = bars;            // synchronous render; wins over `name`
el.icon = undefined;       // clear; falls back to `name` loading

Sizing & color

The rendered SVG uses width="1em" and height="1em", so set font-size on the host or an ancestor. Icon color follows currentColor.

16 24 32 48

API

Member Type Description
name string Attribute/property in <variant>/<icon> form, such as outline/bars-3.
icon IconDef | undefined Property-only override. Assign an imported icon definition for synchronous rendering; set to undefined to resume name loading.
label string Attribute/property label for meaningful icons. Sets the host element's ElementInternals accessible name and default role="img".

Accessibility

Without a label, icons render as decorative content hidden by default through ElementInternals. For a meaningful icon, set the label attribute or property. Raw ARIA attributes are also supported, but host aria-label must be paired with role="img". Add a label only when the icon itself carries information that is not already present in nearby text. 

<button class="btn">
    <neon-icon name="outline/trash"></neon-icon>
    Delete
</button>

<button class="btn" aria-label="Delete">
    <neon-icon name="outline/trash"></neon-icon>
</button>

<neon-icon name="solid/check" label="Confirmed">
</neon-icon>

<neon-icon name="solid/check" role="img" aria-label="Confirmed">
</neon-icon>

<script>
    document.querySelector('neon-icon').label = 'Confirmed';
</script>

site/sections/icons.html.content:
Icons

  • Library
  • Web Component

@neon-kit/icons is the full set of heroicon-derived SVG icons. Each available heroicon ships by variant — outline (24×24 stroked, 1.5px), solid (24×24 filled), mini (20×20 filled), and micro (16×16 filled). Pick a variant via the subpath segment: @neon-kit/icons/outline/bars-3, @neon-kit/icons/solid/bars-3, etc. Each icon is its own ESM module so bundlers tree-shake unused ones. The gallery below renders the same icon definitions through the lightweight internal SvgIcon renderer used by Neon web components.

All icons

    Variant comparison

    The same icon at each variant's native pixel box. Outline and solid share a 24×24 viewBox; mini renders at 20×20; micro at 16×16. Pick the smallest variant that still reads at the size you intend to render.

    outline·24 solid·24 mini·20 micro·16

    Subpath ESM usage

    Preferred for tree-shaking. Each variant lives under its own segment; each icon module exports a default { viewBox, attrs, paths } definition and a precomputed svg string. 

    import outlineMenu from '@neon-kit/icons/outline/bars-3';   // 24×24, stroke 1.5
import solidMenu from '@neon-kit/icons/solid/bars-3';       // 24×24, filled
import miniMenu from '@neon-kit/icons/mini/bars-3';         // 20×20, filled
import microMenu from '@neon-kit/icons/micro/bars-3';       // 16×16, filled
// outlineMenu: { viewBox, attrs, paths }
// import { svg } from '@neon-kit/icons/outline/bars-3' for the precomputed string

    Aggregate ESM usage

    Convenient when you need many icons in one place; pulls the entire variant into the module graph. 

    import { outline, solid, mini, micro } from '@neon-kit/icons';
const menu = outline['bars-3'];
const menuSolid = solid['bars-3'];

// or import a single variant aggregate:
import outlineIcons from '@neon-kit/icons/outline';
outlineIcons['bars-3'];

    Sizing & color

    The SVG inherits currentColor, so any Tailwind text-color utility colors the icon. The rendered SVG is sized in em; size it via CSS font-size on the SVG or any ancestor.

site/sections/jsx-menu.html.content:
Menu — JSX

Menu decorates one button trigger and renders a sibling native popover containing MenuItem buttons. It shares the same roving focus, keyboard navigation, nested-menu coordination, and accessible labelling behavior as <neon-menu>.

Installation

pnpm add @neon-kit/theme @neon-kit/jsx-components @slimlib/jsx

import '@neon-kit/theme/index.css';
import { Menu, MenuItem } from '@neon-kit/jsx-components/menu';

Basic

Pass one button as the trigger and menu JSX as content. The component wires IDs, popovertarget, menu roles, and labelling automatically. 

<Menu
    content={
        <div class="menu__group">
            <MenuItem onClick={createFile}>New file</MenuItem>
            <MenuItem>Open</MenuItem>
            <MenuItem disabled>Delete</MenuItem>
        </div>
    }
>
    <button type="button" class="btn">Actions</button>
</Menu>

Nested menus

Use a MenuItem as another Menu's trigger. → opens the submenu, ← returns to its parent item, and activating a leaf closes the complete open menu tree.

API

  • Menu.children: exactly one HTMLButtonElement trigger.
  • Menu.content: JSX containing owned MenuItem descendants.
  • Menu.placement: block-end, block-start, inline-end, or inline-start.
  • MenuItem.disabled: creates focusable aria-disabled="true" state and suppresses activation.
  • MenuItem.onClick: runs for enabled item activation before leaf menus close.

site/sections/jsx-tooltip.html.content:
Tooltip — JSX

Tooltip is a @slimlib/jsx component that decorates one trigger element with the same popover-based Neon tooltip behavior as <neon-tooltip>. It returns the trigger element, appends the tooltip popover inside it, and keeps the tooltip in Light DOM.

Installation

pnpm add @neon-kit/theme @neon-kit/web-components @slimlib/jsx

import '@neon-kit/theme/index.css';
import { Tooltip } from '@neon-kit/jsx-components/tooltip';

Basic

Pass the trigger as the component child and the informational helper text as content. Default trigger is hover focus. 

<Tooltip content="Persists the current draft.">
    <button type="button" class="btn">Save</button>
</Tooltip>

Placement

Set placement to top, right, bottom, or left.

Rich Informational Content

content accepts JSX for non-interactive structure such as titles, body copy, icons, and keyboard shortcuts. Tooltips are informational helpers and must not contain links, buttons, inputs, or other interactive controls. 

<Tooltip
    placement="bottom"
    content={
        <>
            <div class="tooltip__title">Keyboard shortcut</div>
            <div class="tooltip__body">Open command search.</div>
            <div class="tooltip__meta">
                <span class="kbd-keys">
                    <kbd class="kbd">⌘</kbd>
                    <kbd class="kbd">K</kbd>
                </span>
            </div>
        </>
    }
>
    <button type="button" class="btn">Command search</button>
</Tooltip>

API

Prop Values Default Notes
children One HTMLElement Required The trigger element to decorate.
content JSX child content Required Informational, non-interactive tooltip body.
placement top | bottom | left | right top Adds a matching -<placement> class.
trigger Space-separated subset of hover focus click hover focus Use trigger="" to disable automatic triggers.

Accessibility Pattern

The generated popover receives role="tooltip" and its ID is added to the trigger's aria-describedby ID-reference list, preserving existing description references. The component also wires anchor positioning so hover and focus opens place the popover against the trigger.

Hover waits 400ms before opening and 500ms before closing. Keyboard focus opens and closes the tooltip immediately; click activation is also immediate.

In development builds the component warns when the trigger child is invalid or when a focus tooltip is attached to a non-focusable trigger.

site/sections/kbd.html.content:
Keyboard Shortcuts

The .kbd component renders a keyboard shortcut as a small, flat nameplate. It shares the visual family of .btn (rounded, bordered, top-edge highlight) but is non-interactive and intentionally flatter — no drop shadow, slightly muted surface, tighter proportions, monospaced glyphs.

Single Keys

Square-by-default sign proportions. Single-character keys — letters, digits, and platform glyphs (⌘ ⌥ ⌃ ⇧ ⏎ ⌫ ⎋ ⇥) — render as identical squares regardless of glyph width.

A K 7 ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃ ⏎ ⌫ ⎋ ⇥ ↑ ↓ ← →

Multi-character Labels

Word labels keep the same height and stretch horizontally with even side padding.

Esc Tab Ctrl Shift Alt Enter Space Backspace F12 Page Up

Combos

Wrap individual keys in .kbd-keys for consistent heights and equal visual gaps. Use .kbd-keys__sep for an explicit textual separator (e.g. +) when the convention calls for it.

⌘ K ⌘ ⇧ P ⌃ ⌥ ⌫ Ctrl + Shift + N Alt + F4

Inline With Prose

Keys sit on the surrounding text baseline and inherit font-size, so they scale naturally inside paragraphs and headings.

Press ⌘, to open preferences, or hit ⌘⇧P for the command palette.

Smaller text — Esc dismisses the dialog. The keys scale with the line.

Larger text — ⌘F opens find. Heights still match.

In a Menu

Drop the .kbd nameplate into a menu row in place of the default .menu__shortcut label when you want a heavier, more legend-like trailing affordance.

Menu Component

A panel-styled list of focusable rows for dropdown menus, command palettes, and contextual actions. Items can carry icons (start or end), keyboard-shortcut hints, and chevrons for multi-level menus. Groups are visually divided and may have an optional header. A direct text node or single unclassified element fills the label column; use .menu__label only to group multiple label nodes. RTL flips the layout automatically.

Inline

Timepicker

A typeable time field paired with a popover list of time points rendered at a configurable step (15 / 30 / 60 minutes are common). The field reuses .input's inset-well chrome and the trailing-control language of .combobox / .datepicker; the popover reuses .combobox__popover panel chrome with .combobox__option rows. Optional features: data-step changes the increment, data-seconds adds :SS to the format, and data-tz mounts an IANA timezone selector inside the popover. A combined date + time popover places the day grid and time list side by side (stacked under 640px).

Plain (30-minute step)

Default: a typeable HH:MM input with a clock trigger. The popover lists every half hour from 00:00 to 23:30; click a row to commit and close.

15-Minute Step + Clear

data-step="15" packs the list at quarter-hour granularity. The clear button hides until the field has a value.

With Seconds (1-Hour Step)

data-seconds formats values as HH:MM:SS; data-step="60" shows a shorter list of hourly options.

With Timezone

data-tz renders an inline IANA-zone button next to the time. Clicking it opens a *separate* popover with the same chrome as a single-select .combobox — search at the top, options below, click to commit. The field's zone hint updates live, so a committed time always reads in context without leaving the control.

Field States

Same six-state vocabulary as the datepicker. State hooks land on the inner .timepicker__input; the .timepicker__field wrapper reacts via :has(). Only the field appearance is shown — the time-list popover is unchanged.

Combined Date + Time

.datetime-picker wraps a date and a time field side by side so users can pick both with a single trigger. The shared popover is a .datepicker__popover.-with-time: the day grid sits inline-start, the time list inline-end. On viewports under 640px the panels stack vertically and the popover narrows to fit.

RTL

Logical-property layout flips field order, the trailing trigger, and the combined date+time panel order under dir="rtl".

site/sections/tooltip.html.content:
Tooltip

The .tooltip component is a styled wrapper around the native popover attribute. Because the browser puts every open popover into the top layer, tooltips always paint above siblings — no z-index juggling, no portals, and no breakage from overflow: hidden, transform, or filter on ancestors.

Placement uses CSS anchor positioning. A trigger that invokes the popover with interestfor, commandfor, or popovertarget becomes its anchor, so the position tracks the trigger automatically as layout reflows or scrolls.

Copy-Paste Snippets

Use interestfor for delayed hover and focus hints. Use commandfor for immediate click, Space, and Enter activation. These native invokers are intentionally limited to native interactive elements; use the Web Component or JSX Tooltip when you need arbitrary trigger elements.

Hover / Focus Hint

<button
    class="btn"
    interestfor="tip-save"
    aria-describedby="tip-save"
    type="button"
>
    Save
</button>

<div
    id="tip-save"
    popover="hint"
    class="tooltip -top"
    role="tooltip"
>
    Saves the current document.
    <div class="tooltip__arrow"></div>
</div>

Click / Keyboard Command

<button
    class="btn"
    commandfor="tip-actions"
    command="toggle-popover"
    type="button"
>
    Open details
</button>

<div id="tip-actions" popover class="tooltip -top">
    <div class="tooltip__title">Delete this item?</div>
    <p class="tooltip__body">Removed items can be restored for 30 days.</p>
    <button
        commandfor="tip-actions"
        command="hide-popover"
        type="button"
    >
        Close
    </button>
    <div class="tooltip__arrow"></div>
</div>

Click / Keyboard Commands

Native commandfor handles activation for free: click, Space, and ⏎ all toggle the popover. Click outside or press ⎋ to dismiss.

Saves the current document.
Appears below the trigger.

Hover & Focus Interest

Native interestfor opens popover="hint" tooltips on hover, keyboard focus, and long-press where the platform supports it. The CSS defaults wait 400ms to open and 500ms to close, and can be overridden per trigger.

Reveals on pointer or keyboard focus.

Placement

Four placement modifiers — -top (default), -bottom, -left, -right — driven by position-area.

Rich Content

Because the popover is a regular block container while open, the body can hold any markup: a title with secondary copy, keyboard hints, badges, even interactive elements. Use popover="hint" for transient help and regular popover for command-opened action content.

Choosing an API

  • For description-style tooltips, use role="tooltip" on the popover and aria-describedby="tip-id" on the trigger.
  • For hover and focus help, use interestfor with popover="hint". The CSS component defines --tooltip-open-delay and --tooltip-close-delay on the invoker.
  • For click-open action content, use commandfor with command="toggle-popover" and a regular popover.
  • Native invokers keep the CSS component JavaScript-free but only work on supported native interactive elements. The Web Component and JSX Tooltip keep the previous broader trigger model at the cost of a small JavaScript controller.

Installation

Form participation

The element is form-associated. Submitting the form serialises the current date under its name, including an empty string when the field is blank, matching native input behavior. 


        

    


    

        
Calendar navigation

        

            The popover opens on the day grid. Use the header label to move
            to months and years, or the chevrons to page through the active
            view. Out-of-range days are disabled in the grid.

Menu — Web Component

<neon-menu> is a Light-DOM custom element that adds keyboard behavior to the theme's menu markup: a roving tabindex across <neon-menu-item> rows, arrow-key navigation, Home / End jump, and activation with Enter / Space. Disabled items ([disabled] or aria-disabled="true") remain focusable but cannot be activated. See the rendering-mode ADR.

Installation

pnpm add @neon-kit/theme @neon-kit/web-components

// In your bundle entry:
import '@neon-kit/theme/index.css';
import '@neon-kit/web-components/menu';

Popover-anchored menu

Pair the host element with the native popover API: popovertarget on a trigger button, popover on the <neon-menu>. Open the menu and use the arrow keys, Home, End, Enter, and Space.

New file ⌘ N Open ⌘ O Save (disabled) Project Neon Theme tokens Tooltip notes

Nested popover menus

Nested menus can be composed without extra component code by using a menu item as the native popover trigger for another <neon-menu>. Open the parent, focus Export as, then press →, Enter, or Space to open the child menu. The submenu is authored inside its trigger item so the menu tree shares one root context. Press ← in the child menu to close it and return focus to Export as.

Rename Duplicate Export as PDF document Markdown file HTML page Archive Delete permanently

Each open menu handles its own roving focus. Hover-open behavior remains consumer-owned.

API

<neon-menu> is an autonomous custom element. It does not create any DOM of its own — it consumes the theme's .menu markup and adds keyboard behavior on top. <neon-menu-item> owns item semantics and disabled click suppression.

Markup contract

Rows must be authored as <neon-menu-item class="menu__item"> descendants. Each menu queries its Light-DOM descendants and owns the items whose nearest ancestor <neon-menu> is that menu, so a nested <neon-menu> creates a submenu ownership boundary. The item element does not render its own children, so labels, shortcuts, icons, checkmarks, and chevrons remain consumer-authored markup. One direct text run or unclassified element fills the label column; .menu__label is only needed to group multiple label nodes. Disabled rows use disabled or aria-disabled="true" — both remain in keyboard navigation and click activation is suppressed.

Behavior

  • Provides a default menu role for the host.
  • <neon-menu-item> provides a default menuitem role.
  • Maintains a roving tabindex across items: only the active item has tabindex="0"; the others are -1.
  • On the popover toggle event with newState === "open", focus moves to the first item. The browser's :focus-visible heuristic suppresses the focus ring when the popover was opened by mouse and shows it when opened by keyboard — no manual modality tracking.
  • Queries owned descendant menu items in DOM order and reacts when items are added, removed, or moved.
  • Leaf item activation closes all open popover menus in the same root menu tree after consumer click handlers run.
  • <neon-menu-item> supports popovertarget and popovertargetaction for nested menu composition.
  • A popover menu derives aria-labelledby from its trigger unless the menu already has aria-label or aria-labelledby.

Popover wiring

Pair the host with the popover attribute and a trigger button using popovertarget="<menu-id>" (as in the demo above). Menu items can also use popovertarget to open submenu popovers. For submenus, place the child <neon-menu popover> inside the triggering <neon-menu-item> so the menu tree shares one root context. The theme's .menu CSS provides default placement via position-area: block-end span-inline-end.

Accessibility pattern

Implements the WAI-ARIA Menu and Menubar pattern. The host has a default menu role, each row carries a default menuitem role, and a roving tabindex keeps each menu a single tab stop.

Keyboard support

Key Action
↓ ↑ Move focus to the next / previous item, wrapping at the ends.
Home End Jump to the first / last item.
Enter Space Activate the focused enabled item (calls click()).
→ Open the focused item's submenu and move focus to its first item.
← Close a submenu and return focus to its parent menu item.
Esc Closes the popover (handled by the platform), returning focus to the trigger via the native popover behavior.

Disabled items remain in arrow-key navigation and can receive the roving tabindex, but keyboard and pointer activation are suppressed.

The trigger button keeps its native semantics. On open, focus moves into the menu (first item). On close via Esc or outside dismissal, the native popover behavior returns focus to the trigger.

<neon-multicombobox> is a Light-DOM, form-associated custom element that wraps the theme's .combobox.-multi markup with a multi-select, filterable, keyboard-friendly popover. Add selected to any number of <option> children to seed the initial selection. Toggling rows in the popover does not close it — press Escape or click outside when you're done.

            shows when at least one value is selected; clicking it
            empties the selection and dispatches change.

                        Type
                        Description
                    

                
                
                    

                        values
                        string[]
                        Currently selected values, in option DOM order. Getter returns a defensive copy. Setter accepts any iterable; unknown values are dropped silently. Setting it does not dispatch change.

                        string (read-only)
                        Comma-joined convenience view of values.

                        HTMLOptionElement[]
                        The underlying <option> elements currently selected, in DOM order.
                    

                    

                        options
                        HTMLOptionElement[]
                        All <option> children in DOM order.
                    

                    

                        open
                        boolean
                        Whether the popover is currently open.

                        —
                        Delegated to ElementInternals.

                        input
                        { query }

Accessibility pattern

            WAI-ARIA Combobox pattern
            with list autocomplete, manual selection, and a multi-select
            listbox (aria-multiselectable="true"). Focus
            stays on the search <input role="combobox">
            while open; the highlighted row is tracked with
            aria-activedescendant, leaving the user free
            to keep typing while navigating.

    •

    • 
            
  • Listbox container: role="listbox" with aria-multiselectable="true".
    •

    •

                        Action
                    

                
                
                    

                        
                            Enter /
                            Space /
                            ↓ /
                            ↑
                        
                        On the field: open the popover and focus the search input.
                    

                    

                        
                            ↓ /
                            ↑
                        
                        In the popover: move the active descendant through visible options, wrapping at the ends.

                            End
                        
                        Jump the active descendant to the first / last visible option.

                            Space

Tooltip — Web Component

<neon-tooltip> is an autonomous custom element. Drop it inside the element you want to annotate; it turns its own markup into a popover styled by @neon-kit/theme and wires the parent as the trigger. Renders Light DOM only — see the rendering-mode ADR.

Installation

pnpm add @neon-kit/theme @neon-kit/web-components

// In your bundle entry:
import '@neon-kit/theme/index.css';
import '@neon-kit/web-components/tooltip';

Basic

Plain text inside the element becomes the tooltip body. Default trigger is hover focus; on a <button> parent you also get free click-to-toggle from the platform.

Generated ID

The component generates its own id and points the parent trigger at it with aria-describedby. 

<button aria-describedby="neon-tooltip-k4p9x2m1a">
  Inspect me
  <neon-tooltip id="neon-tooltip-k4p9x2m1a" popover="manual">
    Generated IDs keep this relationship stable.
  </neon-tooltip>
</button>

Placement

Set placement to one of top (default), right, bottom, or left.

Rich content

Use markup for emphasis, icons, and keyboard shortcuts. Do not put interactive elements such as links, buttons, or form controls inside a tooltip.

Non-button parents

Works on any focusable element. Void elements (<input>, <img>) cannot host children — wrap them.

Focus meTooltips work on links too. Focusable span Add tabindex="0" to make a non-focusable element keyboard-reachable.

API

<neon-tooltip> is the popover itself — there is no wrapper DOM. The element it lives inside becomes the trigger.

Attributes

Attribute Values Default Notes
placement top | bottom | left | right top Adds a matching -<placement> class.
trigger Space-separated subset of hover focus click hover focus Set to an empty string (trigger="") to opt out of all automatic triggers and drive the tooltip programmatically.

Popover methods

Method Description
showPopover() Open the tooltip immediately using the native Popover API.
hidePopover() Close the tooltip using the native Popover API.

DOM contract

On connect, the component:

  • Generates an id.
  • Sets popover="manual".
  • Adds the tooltip class plus the placement class (-top, -bottom, -left, -right).
  • Renders a .tooltip__arrow child.
  • Sets a default tooltip role through ElementInternals.
  • Assigns an anchor-name to the parent and references it from the tooltip's position-anchor (existing anchor-name on the parent is reused, not overwritten).
  • Adds the tooltip's id to the parent's aria-describedby ID-reference list.

Accessibility pattern

Implements the WAI-ARIA tooltip pattern. The tooltip is rendered into the browser's top layer via the native popover API, so it escapes overflow and stacking-context ancestors and stays reachable by assistive technology without ARIA portal hacks.

A default tooltip role is applied through ElementInternals. The tooltip body may include presentational markup such as icons, emphasis, and keyboard shortcuts, but it must not contain interactive controls.

The component adds the tooltip's ID to the trigger's aria-describedby ID-reference list so screen readers announce the tooltip text alongside the trigger's accessible name. Existing description references are preserved.

For the focus trigger to fire, the parent must be focusable. In development builds the component logs a console.debug hint when the parent is clearly not focusable (e.g. a <span> without tabindex).

Keyboard focus opens the tooltip immediately and moving focus away closes it immediately. Hover waits 400ms before opening and 500ms before closing. Esc closes an open tooltip when pressed from the trigger. For click-driven tooltips (trigger="click"), clicking the trigger again toggles it closed.

  "repository": {
    "type": "git",
    "url": "git+https://github.com/kshutkin/neon-kit.git",
    "directory": "theme"
  },
  "keywords": [
    "theme",

    "neon"

  "files": [
    "./*.css",
    "components"

  "author": "Konstantin Shutkin",

  "style": "index.css",
  "exports": {
    "./package.json": "./package.json",
    "./index.css": "./index.css",
    "./index": "./index.css",
    "./reset-normalize.css": "./reset-normalize.css",
    "./reset-normalize": "./reset-normalize.css",
    "./theme.css": "./theme.css",
    "./theme": "./theme.css",
    "./theme-dark.css": "./theme-dark.css",
    "./theme-dark": "./theme-dark.css",
    "./components.css": "./components.css",
    "./components": "./components.css"
  },
  "bugs": {
    "url": "https://github.com/kshutkin/neon-kit/issues"
  },
  "homepage": "https://github.com/kshutkin/neon-kit",
  "scripts": {
    "prepack": "npx pkgprn",
    "test": "vitest run --config ../vitest.config.js"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "heroicons": "^2.2.0",
    "prettier-plugin-tailwindcss": "^0.6.14"
  }
}
